subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rajat Mehta <rajat@paymentsai.com>, Aisha Singh <aisha@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Rajat / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Wanted to capture the highlights and next steps so we're aligned. If I missed anything, please flag.

Summary of pain points
- Unit economics: inference spend is the top line driver right now; current cost ~ $0.28	60.32 per transactional call and that's squeezing margins.
- Latency: need p95 under ~100	60ms for real-time scoring in checkout flows.
- Capacity variability: burstiness during peak hours causing cost spikes and occasional tail latency.
- Compliance: certain flows must stay in your VPC/PCI scope.

Current stack (as discussed)
- In-house CPU-based scoring fleet + a GPU-based staging pool for heavy models.
- Kubernetes + custom autoscaler; model hosted via Triton for some endpoints.
- Using an open LLM (variant of Llama family) quantized to int8 for some non-prod workloads.

Success criteria for a pilot/POC
- Reduce per-transaction inference cost to ~ $0.10	60.15 (30	60% reduction) while maintaining or improving latency.
- p95 latency <= 120ms (goal 100ms) for the checkout path at your target QPS.
- Transparent routing and fallbacks for degraded capacity.
- Clear security posture: SOC2, VPC/private option, and KMS for keys.

Our initial recommendations (high level)
- Batching & adaptive batching: per-tenant batching with latency SLO-aware thresholds to improve GPU utilization without increasing user-facing latency.
- KV/prefix caching: cache common prefixes and rate-limited cache hits for repeated prompts to reduce repeated token compute.
- Quantization: you mentioned openness to int8/4-bit testing — we recommend a validation pass comparing int8 vs 4-bit quantization + small eval set to check quality delta.
- Routing: route cost-sensitive flows to quantized model variants and keep critical low-latency flows on higher-performing variants.

Next steps (agreements from today)
1) Redwood: share a preliminary sizing + price estimate and an example cost model for 10M / 20M / 50M monthly requests (attached).
2) PaymentsAI: share a short (one-page) sample of the most common prompts & expected token counts for checkout scoring (for quantization/quality estimates).
3) Schedule technical deep-dive (1h) next week to get into model compatibility, networking/VPC setup, and success criteria for the POC.

Proposed windows: Tue 2026-04-07 09:00	611:00 PT or Wed 2026-04-08 13:00	616:00 PT. Let me know which works.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx (preliminary sizing + cost model)

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—

From: Rajat Mehta <rajat@paymentsai.com>

Cc: Aisha Singh <aisha@paymentsai.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough summary. A few clarifications and extra context so your sizing is realistic:

- Volume: we're seeing roughly 18	622M inference calls/month today; peaks push QPS to ~1.8	62k for short windows.
- Current cost: between $0.25	60.32 per call depending on model variant and whether we hit GPU vs CPU. Our goal is to get to <= $0.12/call for the bulk of traffic.
- Latency: strict internal SLA is 100ms p95 for checkout scoring; other non-critical flows can tolerate higher latency.
- Batching: we do some batching at the ingress layer today but it's conservative because of tail-latency concerns; open to exploring adaptive batching that respects SLOs.
- Quantization: we can run int8 tests in non-prod; if the quality delta is acceptable we're open to production quantization. 4-bit would need stronger QA.
- Compliance: SOC2 is a must for later stages; for the POC we can start with a controlled VPC peering setup.

We're happy to do the 1h technical deep-dive next Wed 2026-04-08 at 14:00 PT. Aisha will join with our infra lead (I'll loop them if helpful).

POC ask: can Redwood provide a short checklist of required infra/networking artifacts for VPC peering and an initial POC success metric doc you can share ahead of the deep-dive?

Thanks — talk next Wed.

Regards,
Rajat Mehta
CTO | PaymentsAI
